tolerance.basis: thin-plate (Kirchhoff) closed form; Kelvin kei kernel

source.doc: Westergaard, H.M. (1926) 'Stresses in concrete pavements computed by theoretical analysis', Public Roads 7(2); reproduced in Hetenyi (1946) and in Kerr, A.D. (1964) 'Elastic and viscoelastic foundation models', J. Appl. Mech. 31(3)
source.table: w(r) = (P ell^2 / (2 pi D)) (-kei(r/ell)), w_max = P/(8 sqrt(D k))
source.access_note: closed form via the Kelvin kei function; kei(0) = -pi/4 re-verified numerically

sha256_scope: sha256 over the archived digitisation artefact (sources/westergaard1926.plate_kei_winkler.csv), i.e. the byte-exact table this entry serves; no page image of the source document is held in-repo, so the anchor does not claim pixel-level provenance

validity_range.note: r/ell > 3 deflection is < 1% of w_max; thin-plate assumption limits r/ell to O(1) for real ice plates

dual_pass.note: pass A = machine-precision transcription of the published closed form; pass B = re-typed at printed precision (5-6 s.f.) with an independent format convention. Human double-keying is NOT claimed.

verification.method: scipy.special.kei(0) vs closed form kei(0) = -pi/4 (=> w_max = P/(8 sqrt(Dk)))
verification.reference: Westergaard (1926) / Hetenyi (1946) infinite plate on Winkler foundation

notes: w_max = P/(8 sqrt(D k)) is the Nevel/Westergaard point-load result quoted for ice plates on an elastic foundation.
